items.title: Classify all 15,710 surviving ordered column-plane parity cores (no κ)
items.body:
## Summary

Answer Open next question 1 of unpaidmoon's #7282 with an exact duplicate-pair deletion criterion for two binary column planes.

```text
joint-type multiplicities
  -> odd-multiplicity support
  -> six distance inequalities + one rank-four test
  -> 15,710 surviving ordered coordinate orbits
```

**Scoped written proof:** deletion order is irrelevant; the tests are necessary and sufficient; a valid final core makes every intermediate deletion safe. The maximum used support is sharply seventeen coordinates. An exact multiplicity normal form covers all original pairs that survive complete deletion.

**Exact finite certificate:** all 524,288 type-labeled core states are enumerated, 467,945 are valid, and the 36 plane-basis changes give 15,710 ordered coordinate orbits. The order of the distinguished columns is preserved. The direct orbit count and a separate literal-matrix Burnside count agree at every support width.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon for #7282's model and deletion question, retaining its #7221/#7139 and earlier image-space lineage. Its exact README and proof at `77b12ac33472b168c5ca6353572d76ed9a76e808` are committed unchanged with SHA256 and Git blob bindings. No predecessor scientific verifier is imported or replayed. Parity reduction, generator-matrix types, the binary simplex code and Burnside's lemma are classical methods.

Card `bit-new-register-model` is explicitly marked changed scope to this local binary geometry question. Selected #7000 and kappa remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** #7282 leaves duplicate-pair deletion open beyond its examples and weight-two census.
- **After:** PROOF.md gives the all-multiplicity criterion and reduction; the new checker independently compares literal binary matrices with the criterion on the complete finite domain, then checks the orbit counts by two methods.
- Normal and optimized warning-strict direct runs passed on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, in 9.66 and 9.69 seconds respectively. These are single local check durations, not performance comparisons.
- Both registered VERIFY.json commands passed, with a 19.84-second total registered replay. Each command has a 120-second timeout. The checks include 1,200 literal deletion fixtures and separate rank, distance, cross-bit and collapse controls.
- Metadata/source pins and exact committed bytes/source history passed. Selected orientation returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY and was not used as a scientific replay.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/column-plane-parity-core/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/column-plane-parity-core/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/column-plane-parity-core
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/column-plane-parity-core --check-source-history
```

On another machine substitute its CPython 3.12 executable. No third-party dependencies are needed. Both modes print PASS_COLUMN_PLANE_PARITY_CORE, with states_checked 524288, labeled_total 467945 and orbit_total 15710.

## Limitations

The all-width statements are written proofs; the orbit numbers are finite computational evidence. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No physical query word, native implementation, supplier admission, improved kappa or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. Unequal-type deletion, deletion of distinguished columns and exchange of the ordered planes are outside this contract.

Overlap checks included live handoffs/open PRs, account history, canonical-main searches and merged-PR searches for the object, general type model and exact quantities. The broad overlap corpus covered 800 open PRs and 7,400 Discussion records. Closed-corpus refresh timed out and sparse local note coverage was incomplete; direct main and merged searches supplemented those gaps. No absence of a match is treated as proof of novelty.

## Open next questions

- Price one surviving six-coordinate core under an explicit arbitrary-input native alphabet and complete producer/consumer/restoration bill. The present geometry gives no paid saving.
- Specify and test a changed deletion or replacement operation on the valid even-multiplicity example whose parity core collapses. New rank, distance, restoration and cost arguments are required.

## Related open work

A fresh check of petalas's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM found no additional PR studying these column-plane parity cores.

- #7282 supplies the column-column model, earlier orbit results and the deletion question answered here; its numerical census is not this ordered parity-core census.
- #7221 supplies further dimension-six coordinate classes and motivates the wider classification; this result classifies survival under one explicit deletion rule.
- #7139 studies the total-image bound at pattern dimension four and its representative geometries; this contribution concerns duplicate-coordinate reduction of the column-column geometry.
- #7138 studies the weight-one no-edge image bound and a reducible column witness; this contribution does not re-establish or alter that bound.

## CI notes

Head `891bc6bedd30af58dd4d3fdf9cf4db35b8fe2334`: **CI did not certify this package.** In [run 43437283229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437283229), [plan job 131925549195](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437283229/job/131925549195) failed at "Onboarding helper tests". The log reports 760 tests, exactly one failure and 24 skips. The failing test is:

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found in the CI verification doc
```

The assertion's missing string and test name were read from the job log; the doc description above abbreviates its full quoted document payload. The same mismatch exists in canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still opens with selected family #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. Neither file is changed by this PR. The package `replay` job was skipped after `plan` failed.

I independently read the job logs and verified the same single failure and 24 skips in [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314), triggered by rohanarun; [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790), triggered by dillona; and [run 43437288667](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437288667), triggered by petalas. These three corroborating runs were checked directly; no claim is made about other runs.

Both registered checks and publication-byte/source-history checks passed locally as recorded above. Hosted package validation remains unrun. No workaround commit, push, workflow rerun or shared-file edit was made; the repository-level navigation repair is left to the maintainers.

items.title: Prove sharp all-column tests with rational width normalizers (no κ)
items.body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. Fixed physical transfer tables may now carry exterior rational functions of the positive column count.

```text
rational residual E(w), f = length(w)
  -> clear a common denominator Q with no positive-width zeros
  -> give component j a polynomial counter of degree deg(Q p_j/q_j)
  -> exact identity cutoff N = sum_j D_j(deg(Q p_j/q_j)+1)
```

Every nonzero complete endpoint has a literal input/output entry witness within widths 1,...,N. A single D-cycle with numerator product_(k=1)^d(f-kD) and denominator f first fails exactly at D(d+1), so the cutoff is sharp. The scalar family 1/f has no fixed finite transfer representation of any dimension; clearing the residual therefore supplies a strict certificate extension.

Credit zxv's PR5441 physical-transfer contract at 11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb and its retained native/phase/compiler lineage. Weighted-automata closure, Newton differences, Kronecker products and constant-coefficient recurrence arguments are classical. The new contribution is this rational-width interface and sharp construction, not an audit of predecessor results or a global literature-priority claim. The changed card scope and exact provenance are recorded in TASK.json and SOURCES.json.

## Evidence

Before, represented recurrence coefficients supplied a fixed-table contract but did not represent 1/f. After, denominator clearing supplies an exact finite residual certificate, with a matching delayed-discrepancy construction.

- Sixteen sharp cycle fixtures, including a first discrepancy at width sixteen.
- All 680 physical word/fixture pairs through width four, with every entry of a two-output, three-input boundary checked by an independent scalar path sum.
- 225 polynomial-counter values and 819 reciprocal-recurrence residue entries.
- Ten controls: six invalid inputs, three forged certificates and one exterior-coefficient boundary.
- Warning-strict normal/optimized direct and registered checks pass on macOS arm64 CPython 3.12.15. The two registered command argument lists took 0.3281 and 0.3282 seconds when timed directly; the registered bundle passed in 1.0066 seconds. These are timeout measurements, not a speedup claim. Generated six-file hash receipts agree.
- Committed bytes, modes and source-history checks pass at 9919c0a3486975fbf82337d97b684ac12324ef2b. Official export integrity/input coverage and both read-only Git-free modes with empty PATH pass; all seven exported files retain their bytes and modes. Syntax, function-size, tabnanny and whitespace checks pass.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/rational-width-certificates/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/rational-width-certificates/verify.py

```

Another CPython 3.12 installation may replace the local interpreter path. Expected scientific marker: PASS_RATIONAL_WIDTH_CERTIFICATES. No predecessor executable is consumed.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal conclusion rests on PROOF.md. The theorem requires characteristic zero, fixed physical letter tables and boundaries, exact equality, and no positive-integer denominator zeros. The executable corroboration uses Q and a sufficient nonnegative-coefficient pole guard; it is not a general root solver or an untrusted-certificate parser. Width zero, arbitrary position dependence, adaptive schedules and approximate tests are outside scope.

No actual selected caller, physical normalization, native/tape implementation, ownership or erasure program, precision/storage bound or complete paid invoice is supplied. No new kappa, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. All five framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review and formal proof-kernel review are unrun or unclaimed. No external static analyzer is claimed.

## Open next questions

- Bind an actual rational-width provider or consumer to the complete residual and exact denominator before applying the certificate to admission. Physical realization and full costs remain blockers.
- Reduce a source-specific cutoff by reducing the rational functions and computing a small pole-free common denominator. This does not minimize every equivalent transfer representation or establish physical savings.

## Related open work

No open PR studying rational-width-normalized transfer identities or this cutoff was found in refreshed live listings, the complete cached open-PR snapshot, handoff claims, and main/merged term searches. Search coverage is bounded and does not prove novelty. PR5441 is the merged question source. PR5376's fixed-coefficient Clifford tests and PR5436's moving-support theorem were read for scope; neither supplies this rational-normalizer cutoff.

The completion refresh read all twelve other account PRs still open and created since the advance CLAIM at 2026-10-30T11:28:04Z. They concern bounded-error frame cuts, encoded Machin sums, a packed TM backend, exact Clifford replay, correlated P104 dirt, prefix-completion performance, Gaussian phase-window counts, rounded native drift, reader caches, nonlinear Eisenstein bounds, box convolution and connector tariffs. None studies this rational-width-normalized transfer identity cutoff or reports a conflicting same-instance value. No extra computations were run to compare predecessor results.

items.title: Research: sharp COPY64 and COPY71 for all-nine-factor uniform P112 columns
items.body:
Rescaling all 52 free entries of one P112 column creates a rank-nine masked completion. This proves that **every exact nine-term complex factorization still has separate COPY cost at least 64**, with sharp power floor `sum rho_j^q >= 8*8^q` for every `0<q<=1`. When all nine terms have nonzero original coordinate projections on both sides, the sharper bounds **71** and `8*8^q+7^q` are also attained.

The family is `K_lambda = XX^T + lambda*(X X_v^T - 4e_v)e_v^T`, for every one of the 112 live columns and every nonzero complex lambda. Lambda=-1 clears the free column entries. All nine factors may vary, with ordinary transpose; the transposed row family follows. Only `research/p112-uniform-column-rank9/` is added.

items.title: Prove the selected tensor phase needs exactly f+1 linear observations (no κ)
items.body:
## Summary

Prove that the absolute diagonal phase of selected MOVE24472's right monomial needs exactly **f+1 binary affine-linear observations** for every positive tensor column count f, even when observations mix columns arbitrarily. Claim type: scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration.

```text
r_j = XOR of coordinates {0,1,2,3,5,6} in column j
b   = XOR of coordinate 7 across all columns
Q_f = f + 3 sum_j r_j + 2b modulo 4
translation periods: every r_j = 0 and b = 0
```

The period subgroup has dimension 8f-1. A sufficient linear statistic must have its kernel inside that subgroup, giving the matching f+1 lower bound. The joint statistic saves f-1 observation bits against retaining the two natural parities separately in every column. This is an information bound, not a physical storage claim; nonlinear evaluation of Q_f itself has a two-bit output.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit CubeJerry #7426, head `172f4535ce8dcff79f626410af845f757c1563be`, for the recipe, source binding, literal implementation **and the existing one-column parity contraction**. Only the complete tensor period subgroup and sharp observation minimum are new. Retain aliromman #5375, #7000's native/Gaussian lineage and antunishdPursuit #6500's parity-expansion context.
